original.target_description: Experiment 5, attitude ambivalence toward public availability of convicted sex-offender lists: implemental one-sided focus versus implemental two-sided focus; specific between-group comparison on journal p. 406 (article p. 11).

notes: Identity independently checked: title The Effects of an Implemental Mind-Set on Attitude Strength; authors Marlone D. Henderson, Yaël de Liver, and Peter M. Gollwitzer; Journal of Personality and Social Psychology 2008, 94(3), 396–411; printed DOI 10.1037/0022-3514.94.3.396. Supplied canonical text is a primary journal article parse with methods, results, references and appendices, rather than an abstract or secondary report. No PDF was supplied; no rendering was possible. Only assigned fields are completed; other fields/sides are placeholders. The requested printed test statistic is t(28) = 2.46. The same comparison prints p < .05 and d = 0.93; p is unassigned and retained here with its bound. Canonical two-column text interleaves the comparison introduction near the bottom of p. 406 with its continuation at the top of that page; es.quote is an exact literal statistic span. Comparison identification evidence (ordered fragments within the introduction): Specific ... comparisons revealed that the implemental mind-set one-sided group ... evidenced a significantly lower amount of ambivalence (M ⫽ 0.16, ... SD ⫽ 1.85) compared to the implemental mind-set two-sided group Allocation candidate 15 + 15 = 30 participants in the two implemental conditions is not certified as final analytic N: the source also excludes one participant but does not specify her condition. Recruitment/allocation total 46 and ANOVA df are not used to resolve this inconsistency or derive N. Printed denominator df 28 is retained only as part of the test statistic.
